contract.success: all 3 hard behavior tests pass for the installed mechanism

spec.name: recruitment-adaptive
spec.question: Across a range of background cue levels, can a receptor mechanism keep recruiting responders to a rising source cue, where a fixed half-occupancy mechanism saturates and collapses?

pass_if.provenance: recruitment_index in [0.4, 1.0] at background=0.0 -- baseline competence, not the discriminator (measured adaptive 0.82, hill 0.58; measured recruitment_index, faithful mechanism-ladder calibration (3-12 seeds))

behavior_tests.name: receptor_gating
behavior_tests.description: Blocking the response abolishes recruitment (receptor-gated mechanisms only)

pass_if.provenance: recruitment_index <= 0.15 at background=400.0, blocked=True -- receptor-mediated recruitment is abolished; the non-receptor static mechanism ignores the block (measured 0.72) and FAILS this test by design (Nasser & Simoni 2009 -- receptor-gated response abolished when downstream signaling is blocked)

behavior_tests.name: recruits_high
behavior_tests.description: Recruits responders at high background (the discriminator)

pass_if.provenance: recruitment_index in [0.35, 1.0] at background=400.0 -- fold-change detection: an adaptive kd rescues recruitment (measured ~0.56, 12-seed mean) where a fixed-kd hill mechanism collapses to 0.00 (Barkai & Leibler 1997, Nature -- robust adaptation via a re-centering set-point; Tu, Shimizu & Berg 2008, PNAS -- fold-change detection in bacterial chemotaxis)

select.rationale: receptor occupancy is catalogued; adaptation is composed on top via occupancy-space chemotaxis with an adaptive kd

audit.revision: recruits_high's one-sided >=0.35 threshold flagged (discrimination drift, unverifiable tightness) -> revised to the two-sided band [0.35, 1.0] mirroring study.yaml -> re-audit clean
